quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 34

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a cell phone.
Changing the radio station or CD.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drivers make about 200 decisions for every mile driven. You must focus all your attention on driving. Any other activity can create a dangerous distraction.

questions.question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights of an emergency vehicle approaching, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Merge into the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren, no matter which direction it is traveling. Drive to the right side of the road and stop immediately until the emergency vehicle passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before stopping on the right side.

questions.question: When can you legally pass on the right side of another vehicle?

options.text: If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
Even if it means driving off the pavement.
On a narrow bridge.
At any time.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right of a vehicle or bicycle that is turning left or waiting to turn left if there is an available passing lane. You may also pass on the right on a multilane road with two or more lanes in the same direction. You can never drive off the pavement to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: If a vehicle with high beams is coming toward you, where should you look?

options.text: Either side of the road
The center of the road
The right side of the road
The left side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side of the road
questions.explanation: If a vehicle is using high beams and does not dim them, look toward the right side of the road. This protects your eyes from the bright headlights and helps you stay on your course until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: Merging traffic
Proceed with caution.
Pedestrian crossing
Come to a full stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow traffic light means you should drive carefully and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Use alternate routes.
Drive the same way as on dry roads.
Increase your following distance.
Avoid crossing bridges or intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between you and the car ahead. Your vehicle will take longer to stop than it would on dry pavement.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other cars.
Drive in the right lane only.
Drive slower than the other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other cars.
questions.explanation: Keeping a safe following distance gives you time to react to problems without sudden braking. This prevents drivers behind you from crashing into your vehicle.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, you should:

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drop onto a low shoulder, reduce your speed without braking. Carefully turn back onto the pavement. Watch for other vehicles when returning to the road.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?

options.text: Communicate with other road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians by signaling when you slow down, stop, or change direction. Use your emergency lights or horn when needed.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Drive faster.
Drive the speed limit with caution.
Not drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when rain, snow, or ice appears on the road. These conditions make roads slippery. You may need to drive slower than the speed limit to stay safe.

questions.question: If traffic lights at an intersection are not working due to a power outage, what should you do?

options.text: Park your vehicle off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to show other drivers what you plan to do.
Turn on your hazard lights and drive through the intersection without stopping.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection as a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers the same way you would at a four-way stop. When it is your turn, go through carefully.

questions.question: If you are in a serious car crash, what should you do?

options.text: Stop.
Call the police.
Check if anyone is hurt.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In a crash, move your vehicle off the road and stop if you can. If anyone is hurt, call 911 right away and help if possible. You must report the crash to police if someone is injured, someone dies, or property damage is more than $1,000 (or more than $200 to government property like signs or guardrails).

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street, what must you do?

options.text: Turn on your hazard lights.
Drive to the nearest side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights or a siren approaches you on a one-way street, drive to the nearest side of the road and stop.

questions.question: What factors affect how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach
Your body weight
How much time passes between drinks
All three of these

questions.correctAnswerText: All three of these
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol content depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Eating before or while drinking slows alcohol absorption slightly, but it cannot prevent impairment if you drink too much.

questions.question: What is the correct order of colors on a traffic light from top to bottom?

options.text: Red, yellow, green
Red, green, yellow
Green, red, yellow
Green, yellow, red

questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green
questions.explanation: On a vertical traffic light, red is always at the top and green at the bottom. On a horizontal traffic light, red is always on the left and green on the right.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with a siren or flashing lights approaches, what must you do right away?

options.text: Drive to the right and stop.
Drive to the right and slow down.
Drive to the right and turn on your hazard lights.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights, sirens, or other warning devices approaches, drive immediately to the right side of the road and stop.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver who arrives first
The driver who arrives last
One driver should go without stopping
One driver should wave others ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first
questions.explanation: At four-way stops, all traffic from four directions must stop. The first vehicle to arrive should go first. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What color are highway signs that show the distance to the next exit?

options.text: Yellow with black letters
Black with white letters
Red with white letters
Green with white letters

questions.correctAnswerText: Green with white letters
questions.explanation: Signs showing directions and destinations are green with white letters or symbols.

questions.question: When must you yield to other drivers?

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley
When a driver on your left reaches an unmarked intersection at the same time as you
When your traffic signal is a green arrow
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley
questions.explanation: You must yield to other drivers when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage. You must also yield to pedestrians on an intersecting sidewalk.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?

options.text: Slow down
Pass with caution
Do not pass
Keep right on hills

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass vehicles in front of you from your direction.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: Upcoming intersections.
Road construction.
A curve in the road ahead.
Changes in traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: A curve in the road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers the road ahead curves to the right.

questions.question: What is the minimum space you should keep between your car and the car ahead?

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
200 feet.
300 feet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least three seconds between your car and the car ahead. Use more distance at high speeds or in bad weather.

questions.question: When may you use your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you have lost control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to alert other drivers if you lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do if you miss your exit on an interstate?

options.text: Stop and make a U-turn.
Get off at the next exit and return to the exit you missed.
Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.
Back up on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and return to the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway. Go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: What must other drivers account for when driving near heavy trucks?

options.text: Heavy trucks need more distance to stop.
Heavy trucks need less distance to stop.
Heavy trucks are quieter.
Heavy trucks are faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy trucks need more distance to stop.
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks need more stopping distance than smaller vehicles. Stay where the truck driver can see you and where your view is not blocked by the truck.

questions.question: What does a red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop at the stop line.
Stop before entering any crosswalk.
Stop before entering the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop at the stop line, before any crosswalk, and before entering the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when a driver behind you wants to pass?

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Slow down to give them room to pass safely.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: Slow down so the other driver has enough space to complete their pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: What should you expect when driving in an area where children are playing?

options.text: They know when it is safe to cross the street.
They will stop at the curb before crossing.
They may run in front of you without looking.
They will not cross unless an adult is with them.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may run in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down in areas where children play. Children may not understand danger and could run in front of your car without looking.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Drive slowly through the intersection.
Stop and then go when the way is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
You may turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop completely. Stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.

questions.question: How should you prepare for hazards ahead on the road?

options.text: Scan the entire road and roadsides continuously.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Focus only on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Scan the entire road and roadsides continuously.
questions.explanation: Find and identify problems before you reach them. Look ahead but also scan the sides of the road. Do not just stare at the center of the road.

questions.question: Before you start the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Before you start the car, buckle your seat belt. Make sure all passengers buckle theirs too. This should be part of your routine every time you drive.

questions.question: A red and white triangular sign means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming.
Look both ways before crossing the intersection.
Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: This is a yield sign. Slow down as you approach the intersection. Let any vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection go first. Be ready to stop if you need to.

questions.question: At night, to avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights, look:

options.text: Straight ahead.
Over your shoulder.
At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming drivers don't dim their lights, look at the right edge of the road. Do not look directly at their headlights. The glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can
Alcohol does not
Even a small amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level greater than 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even a small amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol hurts your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving skills will suffer. You cannot drink and drive safely.

questions.question: When passing on a multi-lane highway:

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before you pass, check that the passing lane is clear. Signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: Leave more space than usual when stopping:

options.text: On a hill.
At an intersection.
At a stop sign.
At a toll plaza.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a hill.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in front of your car when stopped on an uphill slope. If the car ahead rolls backward when traffic starts moving, extra space helps prevent a collision.

questions.question: When entering a street from a driveway, you:

options.text: Must drive slowly to give approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to move out of your way.
Must honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to move.
Must stop and only go when no pedestrians or vehicles are coming.
Can ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop and only go when no pedestrians or vehicles are coming.
questions.explanation: Stop before entering the street from a driveway. Let any vehicles or pedestrians pass first. Stop before crossing the sidewalk area. You must do this by law.

questions.question: To prevent hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Make sure your tires have good tread.
Make sure your tires are inflated properly.
Slow down when driving in the rain.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, make sure your tires have good tread and the right air pressure. Slow down when it rains. Hydroplaning happens most often at higher speeds.

questions.question: When entering a street from a private road, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other drivers you are entering.
Stop with part of your car on the street to alert other drivers.
Drive out fast to merge smoothly with traffic.
Let pedestrians and traffic on the street go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians and traffic on the street go first.
questions.explanation: When you enter a street from a driveway or private road, you must let pedestrians and street traffic pass first.

questions.question: Drive slower than the posted speed limit when:

options.text: Conditions are not perfect.
You see a police car.
Entering a highway with other cars.
You are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Conditions are not perfect.
questions.explanation: When the road is wet or slippery, when you cannot see well, or when anything else is not perfect, drive slower than the speed limit. Even if you are within the speed limit, you can be ticketed for driving too fast for the conditions.
